security_audit.summary: All 37 static findings are false positives. Markdown fences and inline formatting were misclassified as command execution, while relative documentation links and a user-confirmed memory path were misclassified as filesystem traversal. The two URLs are metadata only, and the skill explicitly treats imported data as untrusted.

remediation.issue: Static scanners misclassify Markdown code fences and relative links.
remediation.suggestion: Use scanner rules that distinguish Markdown formatting and documentation links from executable commands and filesystem operations.

remediation.issue: The save-path example includes a user-selected placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Keep saving restricted to the documented memory directory and validate the preference or segment filename before writing.

content.value_statement: Email subscribers may unsubscribe when messages arrive too often or cover irrelevant topics. This skill designs clear topic, frequency, and pause choices that preserve a direct unsubscribe option.
actual_capabilities: Defines topic groups, cadence tiers, channel toggles, and confirmation behavior for a preference center.
Creates an ordered opt-down ladder with frequency reduction, topic selection, pause, and direct unsubscribe.
Maps every preference choice to an explicit suppression or frequency rule.
Produces a SEND N sub-item note with Pass, Partial, or Fail rationale.
Records open questions and labels source information as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
limitations: It does not implement preference pages or configure an email service provider.
It does not store consent or suppression records.
It does not calculate email quality scores or decide the N1 unsubscribe verdict.
It needs stated topics, cadence options, or export data to assess the current experience.

use_cases.title: Reduce newsletter unsubscribes
use_cases.description: Design weekly, monthly, and pause options for a newsletter with a rising unsubscribe rate.

use_cases.title: Plan preference controls for a product launch
use_cases.description: Define topic controls and suppression rules before adding a new promotional email stream.

use_cases.title: Review an existing unsubscribe path
use_cases.description: Document the current path and propose a compliant opt-down ladder with direct unsubscribe access.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic preference center
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a preference center for our monthly product newsletter. Include weekly, monthly, and pause options.

prompt_templates.title: Add topic controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preference page for our customers. Offer product updates, promotions, events, and a monthly digest.

prompt_templates.title: Repair an unsubscribe path
prompt_templates.prompt: Our unsubscribe rate is rising for trial users. Create an opt-down ladder with topic choices, lower frequency, a 90-day pause, and a direct unsubscribe.

prompt_templates.title: Map operational rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a preference-center specification for our ESP. Map each topic, cadence tier, and pause choice to an explicit suppression or frequency rule.

output_examples.input: Create options for a weekly newsletter with product updates and promotions.
output: Topic choices: Product updates and promotions.
Cadence choices: Weekly, monthly, or pause for 90 days.
Rule: Monthly limits eligible sends to one per month.
Direct unsubscribe remains available in one click.
Status: Partial, because no frequency or topic controls are offered.
Recommended order: Reduce frequency, choose topics, pause, then unsubscribe.
Open loop: Confirm whether the ESP can enforce a monthly send cap.

best_practices: Keep the direct unsubscribe option visible and reachable in one click.
Offer only topic and frequency choices the email program can honor.
Map every choice to a tested suppression or frequency rule before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not hide, delay, or require extra steps for unsubscribe.
Do not offer a cadence tier that automation cannot enforce.
Do not treat a topic mute as a full-list unsubscribe unless the subscriber chooses it.

faq.question: Does this skill remove subscribers?
faq.answer: No. It designs preference choices and rules. Your email platform or consent registry applies the resulting records.

faq.question: Can it replace an unsubscribe link?
faq.answer: No. A direct unsubscribe must remain visible and reachable in one click.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your audience, content topics, current cadence, and email platform. An export of current settings is useful but optional.

faq.question: Can it design a pause option?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define a pause duration and the rule that resumes the subscriber at the correct cadence.

faq.question: Does it configure Klaviyo, Mailchimp, or HubSpot?
faq.answer: No. It creates an implementation specification and rule mapping for the platform team to apply.

faq.question: How does it handle consent?
faq.answer: It maps choices to rules but does not become the consent record. Store and honor final records in your approved consent system.
